title: DWARF's CFA is an unwind basis defined with instruction position
summary: The Canonical Frame Address is the logical reference address used by the unwinder to restore the caller's state, calculated from the current register and offset.
applies: Native program crash reporting and DWARF debugging metadata
detail: Different CFA rules can apply to the prologue, body, and epilogue of the same function. Reading the stack snapshot for an instruction requires finding the rule covering that location.
boundary: CFA is not another name for the RBP register, nor does it require that the current stack pointer remains unchanged throughout the function. See DWARF 5 §6.4.
relevance: Explain why a build that does not preserve a fixed frame pointer still gives a trusted call chain.
